clues: A broad river runs down the east side of this town. It marks the line with the town on the far bank.
Winters here are cold with spells of snow, while summers turn hot and humid. Spring and fall sit in between, swinging from warm to cool.
For more than 200 years, two towns took turns as the state capital. Since 1875, this town has held the job on its own.
The writer Mark Twain lived in this city and wrote his most famous books in his house here. He called it the chief of all the beautiful towns he had seen.
The governor of Connecticut works in this town. Its lawmakers meet here to run the state.
